Question ID: ENG1_U04_L06_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: Publication task: Share research about quiet study spaces with ninth-grade students. Which product choice best fits the audience?

answer.text: A. A twenty-page technical report with no headings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too dense for the stated student audience.

answer.text: B. A random list with no source information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication needs clear organization and accurate information.

answer.text: C. A one-page digital summary with clear headings and brief evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This format is easy for students to scan and understand.

answer.text: D. A private note that no one can read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A publication should be prepared for an audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L06_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: Which collaborative role best checks whether source information is accurate?

answer.text: A. Color chooser.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color choice does not verify source accuracy.

answer.text: B. Timekeeper only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Timekeeping may help a team but does not check sources.

answer.text: C. Audience member.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience receives the product, not necessarily checks sources.

answer.text: D. Source checker.

feedback.text: Correct. This role directly supports accurate research publication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L06_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: A team says, "Everyone will do whatever." What is the main problem?

answer.text: A. The plan has too many clear roles.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The plan has no clear roles.

answer.text: B. The audience is explained too carefully.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience is not explained.

answer.text: C. The product is already publication-ready.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The plan is too vague to be ready.

answer.text: D. Responsibilities are unclear, so collaboration may break down.

feedback.text: Correct. Teams need roles so work is organized.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L06_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: Which heading best fits a student-facing research summary about digital announcements?

answer.text: A. How Digital Announcements Help Students Notice Club Deadlines.

feedback.text: Correct. This heading is specific and audience-friendly.

answer.text: B. Random Information That Might Be Somewhere.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This heading is vague and unhelpful.

answer.text: C. Things and Stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not guide the reader.

answer.text: D. The Longest Heading Ever About Every School Topic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unfocused and too broad.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L06_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.04

Prompt: Draft: "Our product will tell people stuff about tutoring." Which revision is clearest?

answer.text: A. Our product has tutoring and people and stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This remains vague.

answer.text: B. Our one-page summary will explain how peer tutoring can support student confidence.

feedback.text: Correct. This clearly names the product, topic, and purpose.

answer.text: C. It will be about things students do.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

answer.text: D. We will make a thing for some audience.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not identify the product or audience clearly.
